hook.en: On a busy highway thousands of vehicles pass every hour, yet only a few accidents happen in a week. When the number of trials is huge and the chance is tiny, the *Poisson distribution* describes the count.
hook.kn: ಹೆದ್ದಾರಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರತಿ ಗಂಟೆ ಸಾವಿರಾರು ವಾಹನಗಳು ಸಾಗುತ್ತವೆ, ಆದರೂ ವಾರದಲ್ಲಿ ಕೆಲವೇ ಅಪಘಾತಗಳಾಗುತ್ತವೆ. ಪ್ರಯೋಗಗಳು ಅತಿ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಭವನೀಯತೆ ಅತಿ ಕಡಿಮೆ ಇದ್ದಾಗ ಪಾಯ್ಸನ್ ವಿತರಣೆ ಎಣಿಕೆಯನ್ನು ವಿವರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ.

title.en: State the Poisson distribution and when it arises
Apply the Poisson approximation to the binomial and fit a Poisson distribution

say.en: On a busy highway thousands of vehicles pass every hour, yet only a few accidents happen in a week. When the number of trials is huge and the chance is tiny, the Poisson distribution describes the count. In this lesson: State the Poisson distribution and when it arises.
Use mean equals variance equals lambda.
Apply the Poisson approximation to the binomial and fit a Poisson distribution.

body.en: A discrete variate $X$ follows the *Poisson* distribution with parameter $\lambda > 0$ if $P(X = x) = \dfrac{e^{-\lambda} \lambda^x}{x!}$, $x = 0, 1, 2, \dots$. It is the limit of $B(n, p)$ as $n \to \infty$, $p \to 0$ with $np = \lambda$ fixed. Examples: printing mistakes per page, defects per metre of cloth, telephone calls per minute, accidents per day.
body.kn: X ಪಾಯ್ಸನ್ ವಿತರಣೆ ಹೊಂದಿದ್ದರೆ P(X = x) = e^(−λ) λˣ / x!. n ಅತಿ ದೊಡ್ಡದು, p ಅತಿ ಚಿಕ್ಕದು, np = λ ಸ್ಥಿರವಾದಾಗ ದ್ವಿಪದದ ಮಿತಿ ರೂಪ. ಉದಾ: ಪುಟದಲ್ಲಿನ ಮುದ್ರಣ ದೋಷಗಳು, ದಿನದ ಅಪಘಾತಗಳು.

points.en: Always positively skewed; skewness falls as λ grows

narration.en: The Poisson distribution has one parameter, lambda. P of x equals e to the minus lambda times lambda to the x, over x factorial. It appears when events are rare but the opportunities are many: misprints on a page, defects in cloth, accidents in a day.

For lambda equal to 2, compute the first few probabilities.
The recurrence formula saves time: multiply the last probability by lambda over x plus one.
Draw the bars. The curve is positively skewed, with a long tail on the right.
Mean and variance are both lambda. That is the quick test for Poisson data.

body.en: Mean $= \lambda$, variance $= \lambda$, s.d. $= \sqrt{\lambda}$. It is positively skewed. Recurrence: $P(x+1) = \dfrac{\lambda}{x+1} P(x)$. To fit a *Poisson distribution* to $N$ observations, take $\lambda = \bar{x}$, find $P(0) = e^{-\bar{x}}$, use the recurrence, and multiply by $N$.
body.kn: ಸರಾಸರಿ = ಪ್ರಸರಣ = λ. ಪುನರಾವರ್ತಿ ಸೂತ್ರ P(x+1) = λ/(x+1) · P(x). ಹೊಂದಿಸಲು λ = x̄ ತೆಗೆದುಕೊಳ್ಳಿ, ನಂತರ N·P(x) ಲೆಕ್ಕಿಸಿ.

problem.en: A book has on average 1.5 printing mistakes per page. Find the probability that a page has at most 1 mistake. (e^(−1.5) = 0.2231)

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A book has on average 1.5 printing mistakes per page. Find the probability that a page has at most 1 mistake. (e^(−1.5) = 0.2231)

say.en: Let us work this out together. A book has on average 1.5 printing mistakes per page. Find the probability that a page has at most 1 mistake. (e^minus 1.5 equals 0.2231).
lambda equals 1.5. P0 equals e^minus 1.5 equals 0.2231.
P1 equals 1.5 times 0.2231 equals 0.3347.
P(X is less than or equal to 1) equals 0.2231 plus 0.3347 equals 0.5578.
So the answer is 0.5578 exact 0.5578.

say.en: Let us work this out together. Fit a Poisson distribution to: x equals 0, 1, 2, 3 with f equals 122, 60, 15, 3 N equals 200.
x̄ = 0 plus 60 plus 30 plus 9/200 equals 99 over 200 equals 0.495 is approximately 0.5, so take lambda equals 0.5.
P0 equals e^minus 0.5 equals 0.6065; f0 equals 200 times 0.6065 equals 121.3.
f1 equals 0.5 times 121.3 equals 60.7; f2 equals (0.5 over 2) times 60.7 equals 15.2.
f3 equals (0.5 over 3) times 15.2 equals 2.5.
So the answer is Expected is approximately 121, 61, 15, 3.
